# Independent audit: full residual containment and strict depth margin

Audited Section 5 of
`candidate 5dd69a77cceb0773`,
with its matrix construction and the full exact-three-fiber hypotheses.

**Result: PASS.** No repair identified.

For one strict actual point P_j in every residual region, the square
matrix C of its affine lambda coordinates has strictly negative
Off-diagonal entries, positive diagonal, and column sums one. The
previously proved geometric-series inverse is entrywise nonnegative.
Because 1^T C=1^T, also 1^T C^(-1)=1^T. Thus every nonnegative lambda
vector of sum one maps to a nonnegative theta vector of sum one.
The entire standard lambda simplex, which corresponds exactly to -T,
lies in conv(P_j) subset A. This proves actual set containment, not only
a volume inequality. Reflection preserves volume, so |−T|=V>=b.

Every A cap v_i.x>=-1 contains the entire -T, giving U_i>=V>=b>0.
The raw critical equality is Q=U_i+q_i because there are exactly three
contributing fibers and the B captures have zero d-volume. Proper full
fibers justify ordinary d-volume and every nonvertical boundary is null.

For the tilted actual cap v_i.x>=theta*z, the A threshold is -theta
and the B threshold theta. Their continuous volume difference tends
to -b and a at the two infinities. Hence at some finite theta they
capture equal volume t. Criticality of the original cap at the actual
middle source gives U_i<=2t, so t>0. Actual midpoint compatibility of
the two captured sets puts their Minkowski midpoint inside the unchanged
middle cap. Brunn--Minkowski at equal positive volumes gives q_i>=t.
Consequently U_i<=2q_i and U_i<=2Q/3. This is a comparison among actual
containing ambient halfspaces, with no rounded center or assumed
first-variation identity.

The A caps and middle caps each cover their entire continuous body.
One therefore contains the corresponding ordinary centroid. Ordinary
Grunbaum yields Gamma*a<=2Q/3 and Gamma*k<=Q-b. Adding b gives

    M<=5Q/(3Gamma)-(1-Gamma)b/Gamma<5Q/(3Gamma).

Strictness uses b>0 and Gamma<1. Division by the positive masses gives
Q/M>3Gamma/5>Gamma/2. The source's d>=2 scope satisfies every condition;
there is no degenerate-fiber assertion or missing boundary mass.
Thus a source at or below the OC target in this exact canonical critical
regime must lack at least one residual region. The note correctly leaves
the remaining residual patterns unresolved.

## Closed-corner strengthening

The latest extension also PASSes. If every closed corner C_j is nonempty,
its chosen column has diagonal at least one and off-diagonals nonpositive,
with column sum one. Writing C=D-N gives, in each column,
sum(N D^(-1))=1-1/C_jj<1. Thus the same finite-dimensional geometric
series converges and gives C^(-1)>=0 even with vanishing off-diagonal
entries. The column-sum inverse identity is unchanged, proving actual
-T containment without a strict residual-volume assumption.

No strict inequality |conv(P_j)|>|T| is inferred in this extension.
The previously audited depth margin only needs the nonstrict containment;
its final strictness comes from b>0 and Gamma<1. Therefore a source at
or below Gamma*M/2 has some CLOSED corner empty. Compactness then gives
strict separation from that closed corner, as checked in the separate
separation audit. Boundary-only corner points are fully retained.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
